# macosdefaults Provider

Manages macOS preferences through the `defaults` tool on the machine running Terraform. It only works on macOS, and needs no credentials.

`scope` sets the default for every resource and data source; each can override it. Which scopes a run can use depends on who runs it: `system` needs root, and the others need a normal user.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    macosdefaults = {
      source  = "registry.terraform.io/demon/macosdefaults"
      version = "~> 0.1"
    }
  }
}

# The provider runs /usr/bin/defaults as the user running Terraform, so it
# only works on macOS. It takes no credentials.
provider "macosdefaults" {
  # Default scope for resources and data sources that don't set their own:
  # "user" (the default), "current_host", or "system" (needs `sudo terraform`).
  scope = "user"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `scope` (String) The default scope for every resource and data source that doesn't set its own: `user` for the current user's preferences, `current_host` for the current user's preferences on this Mac only (`defaults -currentHost`), or `system` for machine-wide preferences in `/Library/Preferences`. `system` requires running Terraform as root, and the other scopes require *not* running as root. Defaults to `user`. Set it to `system` in a configuration you apply with `sudo`.
